answer: A per-identity work deposit defeats Sybils: each agent must redeem one uniquely registered computation keyed to a fresh attestation root, and the registry stores the output, so an identity burns one unused solution like mining a karst hollow. Honest agents withdraw the deposit, so their cost is opportunity cost, while a farm must fund thousands of concurrent deposits and distinct attestation chains. Unlike a vine that can be cloned, every branch needs its own root, so the attacker's bill grows linearly while influence does not. Duplicates forfeit the deposit, a penalty that empties the lagoon.
